podcast.body: Later in the same year as "King of America," Costello reformed The Attractions for this album, which was recorded near live in the studio, loud, and with as few takes as possible. The album's bruising and raucous sound was later identified by critics as a kind of proto-grunge, predating the coining of the term itself. The most remembered song from this album, however, was the slower, sinister "I Want You." "the album was later tagged by critics as a kind of proto-grunge before that term had even been coined."

podcast.body: This album marked a reunion with his band, The Attractions, and was seen by fans as the closest return to his "old school Elvis" sound after years of musical experimentation. It also features "I Want You," which is the longest song in his catalog. "The album was called Blood and Chocolate. And this was the closest thing to old school Elvis fans had heard in a long, long time."
